answer: Any agent claiming work must post a timber-sized bond into a shared vault before submitting proofs. A random challenger then issues a live inference task: the claimant must reproduce a hidden pearl of output within a tight latency budget, and a panel cross-checks. Passing refunds the bond; failing slashes it to the challenger and the panel. Because each fake identity must fund a fresh bond and survive a genuinely hard compute challenge, forgery costs scale linearly with spawned accounts, making mass sybil creation economically irrational.
